messages.content: You design amateur rockets that fly on certified commercial motors. Work through the design, check it with the tools, and give the final design as JSON inside <design> tags. Only report results the tools returned.
Hi, we'd like an apogee near 375 m. 30 mm OD max. It usually blows around 3 m/s at our field. Our pad has a 1 m rod.

messages.reasoning_content:
1. Understand: apogee about 375 m, so the band is 375 m ±5%. Body outer diameter at most 30 mm (0.030 m). Wind about 3 m/s. Rail is fixed at 1 m, shorter than a usual club rail. Landing speed is not stated, so I assume 6 m/s. Single stage, vertical, sea level.
2. Feasibility: drag-free speed for 375 m is sqrt(2 * 9.81 * 375) = 86 m/s. That is C-class impulse on a small airframe. The 1 m rod is the tight part: average thrust has to get the rocket through 15 m/s before the rod ends. I need motor thrust and diameter before I commit.

2. Feasibility: the C6 is 8.8 N*s at 4.8 N average and 14.1 N peak, 18 mm. The C11 is the same 8.8 N*s but 11.3 N and 24 mm, so the tube has to grow toward the 30 mm cap and drag goes up. The D10 lookup returned a D10W at 18.7 N*s, and 18.7 / 8.8 = 2.1 times a C, which would fly well past 375 m inside a 30 mm body. The D21T is 19.6 N*s. The C6 is the impulse match; the 1 m rod is the open question because peak thrust is much higher than the average.
3. Size: guessed liftoff mass 0.045 kg. Thrust-to-weight = 4.8 / (0.045 * 9.81) = 10.9. On the 1 m rod, average acceleration is (4.8 - 0.045 * 9.81) / 0.045 = 97 m/s^2, so sqrt(2 * 97 * 1) = 13.9 m/s using average thrust. That is under 15 m/s, and only the 14.1 N spike can save it. Descent mass is about 0.045 - 0.011 = 0.034 kg. For a 5 m/s landing at Cd 0.8 the area is 2 * 0.034 * 9.81 / (1.225 * 0.8 * 5^2) = 0.027 m^2, diameter sqrt(4 * 0.027 / 3.1416) = 0.19 m. I'll fit a 0.20 m chute.
4. Draft: 22 mm cardboard tube, under the 30 mm cap, ogive nose, three balsa fins, 18 mm mount, Estes C6 plugged, chute at apogee. Conditions are the stated 3 m/s wind and 1 m rod.

4. Check: the simulator gives apogee 374.9 m. The goal is 375 m, and 375 - 374.9 = 0.1 m, against an allowed half-band of 0.05 * 375 = 18.8 m, so altitude passes. Rail exit is 21.3 m/s, above 15, even though the average-thrust estimate was 13.9 m/s; the spike covered the short rod. Thrust-to-weight is 11.2, margin 1.99 cal, landing 4.6 m/s under 6. Body diameter 22 mm is under the 30 mm cap. Wind was 3 m/s and the rod was 1 m.
5. Fix: no fix was needed.
6. Uncertainty: 374.9 m is sitting on the target, so a heavier paint job or a rougher finish will drop it out of the 5% band. The 1 m rod result depends on the C6 thrust spike; a slower-lighting motor of the same impulse could leave the rod under 15 m/s. Chute Cd is a model 0.8, and the landing number will move if the real canopy differs. Margin is 1.99 cal in a 3 m/s wind, enough, but a stronger gust will weathercock it.
messages.content:
C6 on a 22 mm cardboard rocket, 0.46 m long, chute opening at apogee.
On the 1 m rod in 3 m/s wind the apogee is 374.9 m and the landing is 4.6 m/s.
Rail exit is 21.3 m/s at 1.99 cal, and the tube is under the 30 mm cap.
